title: A projective family with finite generic fibre is generically finite
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$, and let
$D\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be
projective.
If $D_K$ has dimension at most zero, this morphism is finite after
restriction to a nonempty open of $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

proof.text: Projectivity implies properness by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Let eta:Spec K -> Spec A be the displayed fraction-field map. Properness is stable under base change by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], so the projection D_K -> Spec K is proper and hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] with the dimension hypothesis: D_K is locally Noetherian, locally Artinian, compact and discrete, and its underlying set is finite.

source.place: exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_generic_fibre, first four instance arguments; the same argument works with the given fraction field K

proof.text: Choose the point p of the nonempty spectrum of the field K. For every y with f(y)=eta(p), the point-lifting corollary of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] gives z in D_K mapping to y and p (Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback). Thus the ordinary fibre f^{-1}({eta(p)}) is contained in the range of D_K -> D. That range is finite by Step 1, hence the ordinary fibre is finite. This avoids identifying K with a particular residue-field implementation.

Apply [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near], the Mathlib theorem exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_finite_preimage_singleton, to the proper morphism f at eta(p) with the finite ordinary fibre of Step 2. Obtain an open U containing eta(p) with IsFinite (f restricted to U). This theorem does not require a locally Noetherian base.

proof.text: Since eta(p) belongs to U, the set U is nonempty. Return U with this explicit witness and the finite restriction from Step 3.
